claim_verdicts.rationale: This is a surviving direct incoming-to-Darwin response pair. Kemp's letter is an account of the seed discovery and its geological setting; Darwin explicitly acknowledges that the paper reached him and then answers particular points from it, including the missing depth, the proposed former damp climate, and the plant description. The outgoing editorial notes explicitly establish its year from the relationship to Kemp's 2 October letter and identify that letter as the source of the location description.

evidence.quote: At your request, I forward the following account of the discovery, and description of the place where that ancient seed was found,
I write a line to inform you that your paper has reached me safely.—
Will you inform me, soon about how many feet the layer with the seeds was above the present level of the nearest part of the present river.—
I think your speculation about the former dampness of climate too bold—

claim_verdicts.caveats: The response establishes that the paper was available to Darwin by 9 October, but neither the packet nor the metadata establishes the actual receipt date. The outgoing date is editorially supplied as 9 October [1843] (XML when=1843-10-09); the year is derived from the 2 October relationship. Kemp's quotations and opinions remain Kemp's voice. The editorial notes refer to Lindley and Henslow communications, but those are outside this pair and do not add receipt evidence here.

claim_verdicts.rationale: This is a surviving direct incoming-to-Darwin response pair. Kemp's 4 November letter describes his disappointment, accepts that the evidence may be confounded, and releases his papers; Darwin's response specifically praises the tone of that last letter and proposes a concise statement, while asking for the Babington letter that Kemp's exchange supplied. The editorial notes explicitly identify 4 November as the related letter and resolve the response date to the first Thursday after it.

evidence.quote: I am only sorrie upon your account, as you have taken so much interest, and trouble in the matter,
As my papers are of no further use I am no way ancious about having them returned.
Allow me to express my respect at the pleasant tone of your last letter,
With your permission I will draw up a short statement with as little theory as possible & will send it you for your approval.
Would you please return me Mr Babington’s letter, that I may quote it.—

claim_verdicts.caveats: The response establishes availability of Kemp's 4 November letter by 9 November, not its actual receipt date. The outgoing date is editorially supplied as [9 November 1843] (XML when=1843-11-09), based on the 4 November and 10 November exchange; the 10 November letter and other preceding context were not in this six-letter packet. Darwin's references to Lindley and Babington concern third-party material and do not make their voices Darwin's.

claim_verdicts.rationale: This is a surviving direct incoming-to-Darwin response pair. Kemp supplies further particulars about the discovery and says that certificates are enclosed; Darwin's response says he has added the particulars last sent to Kemp's paper and directly addresses the testimonial Kemp sent. The outgoing editorial notes explicitly identify the 4 December letter as the source of both the added details and the testimonials.

evidence.quote: I have enclosed certificates respecting those men, and could obtain 100 as good—
with the particulars last sent added.—
I am sorry you thought it adviseable to send me a testimonial of yourself—

claim_verdicts.caveats: The response establishes availability of the 4 December letter by 7 December, not the actual receipt date. The outgoing date is editorially supplied as 7 December [1843] (XML when=1843-12-07), with a 7 DE 7 | 1843 postmark noted. The incoming record is marked 2pp encl; the enclosures themselves are not reconstructed in the packet, so the testimonial about Kemp is supported by the outgoing text and editorial note rather than by a full reading of the enclosure. Kemp's opening also refers to Darwin's 1 December letter, which is prior context outside this pair.

issues.text: All three known_by_date values are conservative upper bounds established by Darwin's surviving response. Incoming composition dates do not establish when Darwin received the letters, and the packet has no actual receipt dates.

The XML dates are constrained to 1843-10-09, 1843-11-09, and 1843-12-07, but all three outgoing displayed dates include editorially supplied year or date components. 711F is additionally resolved from the surrounding 4 and 10 November exchange.

720 is marked 2pp encl and refers to certificates; the enclosures are not present as reconstructed prompt text. Claims about their contents are limited to the incoming and outgoing references plus the editorial note.

Editorial notes cite other Kemp, Lindley, Henslow, Babington, and 10 November communications. Those references support editorial linkage and chronology, but the six specified letter bodies are the only texts reviewed here; no absent text was treated as read or as additional evidence.

699, 711, and 720 are Kemp letters; only 701F, 711F, and 720F supply Darwin's surviving response voice. Third-party opinions quoted or summarized in Darwin's letters remain attributed to those third parties.

The preserved XML files contain the sender, recipient, date, physical-description, and provenance metadata, while their body divs are empty; the full transcriptions reviewed for quotations are the preserved HTML packet bodies.
